video_metadata.working_title: ALASKA 1993 Cold Case Solved After 26 Years — Justice for Sophie Sergie
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: Sophie Sergie, a 20-year-old Yup'ik woman from Pitkas Point, was sexually assaulted and murdered in a Bartlett Hall bathroom at the University of Alaska Fairbanks in April 1993; nearly 26 years later genetic genealogy, through a DNA profile uploaded by his aunt, led Alaska State Troopers to Steven Harris Downs, a nurse in Auburn, Maine, who was convicted in 2022 and sentenced to 75 years.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: grief turning into dignified, hard-won justice; quiet outrage at how long Alaska Native families wait

protagonist._instructions: The main character of your story - can be hero, villain, or antihero. Fill with verified facts only.
protagonist.full_name: Sophie Sergie (victim, heart of the story)
protagonist.occupation_or_status: University of Alaska Fairbanks student on leave that semester; she had taken time off from college to save money for orthodontic work [12][18]
protagonist.location: Home: Pitkas Point, a small Yup'ik community near St. Mary's in western Alaska (Kusilvak Census Area, population 120 in 2020) [31]. Killed in Bartlett Hall, UAF, Fairbanks [1][5].
protagonist.physical_description: Not used beyond the public photo released by Alaska State Troopers [19]
protagonist.background_brief: Yup'ik woman from Pitkas Point [27]; former UAF student; when in Fairbanks she stayed with her friend and former roommate Shirley Akelkok [12]. Mother: Elena Sergie [22]. Brother: Alexi Sergie [1].
protagonist.psychological_profile: Described by her friend Shirley Akelkok at trial as a responsible student who was not a partier [12]. Prosecutors at sentencing called her a 'young vibrant woman' [2].
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: She flew to Fairbanks on April 24, 1993 for an orthodontic appointment and to visit friends; she stepped out to smoke a cigarette shortly after midnight [12][34].

victims_or_targets._instructions: People affected by the protagonist's actions. Include 3-5 key figures minimum.

individuals.name: Sophie Sergie
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Victim; had no known connection to Downs, who told police he never knew her [7][18]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Sexually assaulted, stabbed and shot in the back of the head with a .22-caliber gun; found in a bathtub in a second-floor women's bathroom of Bartlett Hall on April 26, 1993 [5][7][24]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Saving money for orthodontic work; not a partier, according to her friend [12]

individuals.name: Elena Sergie
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Waited about 26 years for an arrest; took part in the 2019 arraignment by telephone with the help of a Yup'ik language interpreter [22]

individuals.name: Alexi Sergie
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Tried to deliver the family impact statement by phone from Western Alaska at the September 2022 sentencing; the call dropped and he did not rejoin [1]

collective_victims_if_applicable.group_description: Missing and murdered Indigenous women and girls (MMIW/MMIWG) in Alaska
collective_victims_if_applicable.total_number_affected: Urban Indian Health Institute 2018 report: Alaska had 52 MMIWG cases in its data, the fourth-highest state [26]; Alaska DPS 2022 legislative testimony: about 1,300 missing persons on record going back to the 1960s, 203 female, 55 identified as Alaska Native [28]
collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: Long waits, data gaps, unsolved cases; advocates cited Sophie's case as an exception rather than the rule [28]

supporting_characters._instructions: Investigators, accomplices, witnesses, family members - anyone who plays a significant role.

characters.name: Steven Harris Downs
characters.role_in_story: Convicted killer; 18-year-old UAF freshman living in Bartlett Hall in 1993; later a nurse living in Auburn, Maine [1][5][9]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Denied knowing Sergie; said he recognized her only from posters after her death; denied owning a gun as a freshman [18][6]. Convicted February 2022; sentenced to 75 years; maintains his innocence; appealed [1][21]
characters.notable_quotes: 'There has to be a mistake' (2019 recorded police interview, played at trial) [18]

characters.name: Randel (Randy) McPherron
characters.role_in_story: Alaska State Troopers cold case investigator and lead detective [6][11]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Led the cold case work that sent the profile to Parabon NanoLabs; acknowledged in 2021 that some information in sworn search-warrant affidavits was erroneous [11]

characters.name: CeCe Moore
characters.key_actions_they_took: Connected the crime-scene DNA to the GEDmatch profile of Downs' aunt [6]

characters.name: Shirley Akelkok
characters.role_in_story: Sophie's friend and former roommate; Sophie stayed with her in Bartlett Hall [12][13]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Testified on the first day of trial in January 2022 [13]
characters.notable_quotes: Paraphrase only: there were basically two groups at UAF, heavy partiers or not, and Sophie was not a partier [12]

characters.name: Nicholas Dazer
characters.key_actions_they_took: Re-interviewed by cold case investigators around 2010 after they learned he had been fired as a dorm security guard for having a firearm; troopers collected his DNA at his Portland, Oregon law office; at some point told investigators Downs owned a .22 in 1993 [24][15]. At trial recalled an H&R .22 and a derringer, said he could not imagine Downs connected to the crime, and said he might be misremembering details of the gun [14]

characters.name: James (Jim) Howaniec
characters.key_actions_they_took: Argued alternate male DNA (hairs and saliva) did not match Downs, no fingerprints, gun seized in 2019 not the murder weapon, and that the roommate deflected suspicion; presented alternative suspects [14][17][25]

characters.name: Jenna Gruenstein
characters.role_in_story: Prosecutor, Alaska Office of Special Prosecutions (single-source on role; KUAC tag) [3]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Prosecuted the case at trial and sentencing

characters.name: Judge Thomas Temple
characters.key_actions_they_took: Presided over trial and sentencing; imposed 67 years for murder plus 8 for sexual assault [1][2]
characters.notable_quotes: Paraphrase: no sentence the court could impose would adequately restore Ms. Sergie's surviving family or her extended support network [2]

chronological_timeline._instructions: List every significant event with exact dates when possible. This is the backbone of your script.

events.what_happened: Sophie Sergie, 20, flew to Fairbanks for an orthodontic appointment and to visit friends, staying with friend Shirley Akelkok in Bartlett Hall

events.date: Shortly after midnight, early Monday, April 26, 1993
events.what_happened: Sophie went out to smoke; her friend suggested the women's tub room with its exhaust vents to avoid the cold outside; she was last seen alive
Janitorial staff found her body in a bathtub; she had been sexually assaulted, stabbed and shot in the back of the head with a .22-caliber gun
events.significance: Discovery; biological evidence and a .22 bullet collected; no weapon found

events.what_happened: Investigators developed a DNA profile of the unknown suspect from biological evidence collected in 1993
events.significance: The evidence that would solve the case

events.what_happened: Profile reprocessed with more advanced technology and entered into the FBI's national DNA database (CODIS); no identification resulted
events.significance: The database could only find people already in it

events.what_happened: Cold case investigators re-interviewed Downs' former roommate after learning he had been fired as a dorm security guard for having a firearm; they collected his DNA at his law office. At some point (date not specified in sources) he told investigators Downs had owned a .22 in 1993
events.significance: First documented pointer toward Downs' gun, but no DNA link yet

events.what_happened: Arrest of Joseph DeAngelo in the Golden State Killer case through genetic genealogy
events.significance: Inspired Alaska troopers to try the technique

events.what_happened: AST cold case unit sent the unknown profile to Parabon NanoLabs
CeCe Moore linked the crime-scene DNA to a GEDmatch profile uploaded by Downs' aunt (reported as living in Vermont); family-tree work pointed to her nephew Steven H. Downs
Investigators searched Downs' home and obtained a DNA sample sent to the Maine State Police Crime Laboratory; it matched the crime-scene DNA

events.location: Near the Auburn Fireside Inn, Auburn, Maine
events.what_happened: Downs, 44, a nurse, arrested by Maine State Police with Alaska State Troopers; charged with first-degree murder and sexual assault
Downs told investigators he recalled the murder but never knew Sergie, recognized her from posters, denied owning a gun as a freshman, and said 'there has to be a mistake'
Downs dropped his fight against extradition to Alaska
Downs pleaded not guilty; bail set at $1 million; Sophie's mother Elena took part by phone with a Yup'ik interpreter
events.significance: Family present at the start of the court process

events.what_happened: Trooper McPherron acknowledged erroneous information in search-warrant affidavits; the case proceeded despite the pandemic; defense motions challenging the DNA evidence were denied
Judge ruled the defense could present evidence about three alternative suspects
Trial opened; Shirley Akelkok testified
events.significance: Trial begins nearly 29 years after the murder

events.what_happened: Former roommate Nicholas Dazer and Downs' college girlfriend testified
Recordings of three 2019 interviews with Downs played for the jury
Defense presented witnesses and alternate-suspect theories, including that a gun seized in 2019 was not the murder weapon
Twelve-person jury convicted Downs, 47, of first-degree murder and first-degree sexual assault (deliberations reported as two to three days)
Judge Thomas Temple sentenced Downs to 67 years for murder and 8 for sexual assault, 75 total; prosecutors had sought 99 plus 8; Alexi Sergie's phone call dropped before his statement
Downs appealed his convictions and sentence, citing among other things the denial of a joint COVID-era continuance; sought a public defender
events.significance: Current legal status: appeal filed; outcome not found as of October 2026

cold_open_material._instructions: The most dramatic moment of your story - this will be your hook.

the_moment.exact_location: Bartlett Hall, University of Alaska Fairbanks
the_moment.what_is_happening: A 20-year-old Yup'ik woman visiting a friend steps out of the room to smoke a cigarette, toward the women's tub room, to stay out of the cold
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: She was found that afternoon in a bathtub; the man convicted lived in the same dormitory and walked free for almost 26 years
the_moment.ironic_twist: He became a nurse in Maine; the DNA that named him came not from him but from his aunt's genealogy upload

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who killed Sophie Sergie in a dormitory full of students, and why did it take nearly 26 years to answer?

the_method._instructions: How did the protagonist do what they did? Technical details that can be explained to a general audience.
step_by_step_explanation: Biological evidence collected in 1993 yielded a DNA profile in the late 1990s [24]
In 2000 the profile was entered into CODIS, which only finds people already in the criminal database [24]
In July 2018 troopers sent the sample data to Parabon NanoLabs [8]
Parabon produced a SNP profile and uploaded it to GEDmatch, a public genealogy database [8][6]
A match to a profile uploaded by Downs' aunt pointed to a family; genealogists built family trees to narrow to her nephew [6][9]
Investigators obtained Downs' DNA in Maine in February 2019 and the state lab confirmed the match [6][7]
the_method.why_it_worked: A relative had voluntarily uploaded DNA to a public site that, in 2018, police could search [9]

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: The FBI's national DNA index: it can only recognize a person already in it, like a phone book that lists only people who have been arrested or convicted
A much larger read of the DNA, hundreds of thousands of markers, that can be compared with consumer genealogy tests to find cousins
A free website, launched in 2010, where people upload consumer DNA results to find relatives

the_method.scale_of_operation: One aunt's upload, months of family-tree work, one confirming sample

systemic_failure._instructions: What institution, system, or authority failed to prevent this?
systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: Not a single failure; time and technology. Also a broader systemic pattern of unsolved cases of Alaska Native women
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: DNA could not identify a person with no criminal record; the dorm canvass did not produce the killer
specific_incompetence_examples: In 2021 the lead trooper acknowledged erroneous information in sworn search-warrant affidavits [11]
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The answer had been in the evidence since 1993; the man lived in the same building

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Alaska State Troopers (Alaska Bureau of Investigation cold case unit), with Maine State Police
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: Defense presented three alternative suspects at trial; no person was wrongly charged [25]
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: Genetic genealogy match to Downs' aunt on GEDmatch [6][9]
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: Leaving his DNA at the scene

the_confrontation._instructions: The arrest, raid, or climactic moment when everything collapses.
the_confrontation.location: Near the Auburn Fireside Inn, Auburn, Maine [23]
the_confrontation.scene_description: Maine State Police, working with Alaska State Troopers, arrested Downs, 44, near his home [5][23]
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: In recorded interviews he denied knowing Sergie and said 'there has to be a mistake' [18]
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: He had become a nurse, a caregiver [1][9]

legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: Friend Shirley Akelkok; roommate Nicholas Dazer on the .22; recordings of Downs' 2019 interviews [12][14][18]

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: Not delivered; the phone call dropped [1]
victim_impact_statements.emotional_impact: The family's voice was nearly absent from the final hearing

legal_resolution.sentence_received: 75 years: 67 for murder, 8 for sexual assault; reported eligible for discretionary parole after 25 years (single-sourced) [1][2]
legal_resolution.protagonist_statement_in_court: Maintains his innocence (details of any allocution not verified) [2]
legal_resolution.current_status: Serving his sentence in Alaska custody (facility not verified); appeal filed with the Alaska Court of Appeals in October 2022; no decision found as of October 2026 [21]

universal_stakes.why_this_matters_to_viewer: A young woman was killed in a place that should have been safe, and her family waited decades
universal_stakes.how_this_could_happen_to_them: A dorm, a cigarette break, a neighbor down the hall
universal_stakes.lesson_or_warning: Evidence kept properly can speak decades later; Indigenous victims deserve the same persistence
